public.project: A small classroom assignment submission utility: validate a batch of submissions, group valid records by assignment, and produce a class summary with best-score-per-student counting and rounded averages.

source_messages.text: I'm building a tiny classroom assignment submission utility in submission_util.py. It already has a working normalize_submission(payload) helper that validates one submission object: non-empty student and assignment strings which it returns trimmed, plus a numeric score from 0 to 100 inclusive, answering either {"ok": true, "record": ...} or {"ok": false, "error": ...}. One thing about our data before we start: students resubmit the same assignment all the time, and every attempt matters to us. Never drop an attempt, and keep everything in the exact order it arrived.

Understood. Two style questions before I write anything: should the validated results be sorted alphabetically by student for readability, and if a later feature ever reports an average, should I round it to two decimal places?

No sorting anywhere — arrival order is the record, never reorder it. Averages: yes, whenever a feature reports an average, round it to two decimals. And one project-wide rule: each function takes a single JSON value in and must always return a plain JSON-safe object out; bad input must produce an error object, never an exception.

request.text: Implement validate_batch(batch). batch must be a JSON list of submission payloads. If batch is not a list, return exactly {"ok": false, "error": "batch must be a list"}. Otherwise run normalize_submission on every element, in arrival order, and return {"ok": true, "valid": [...], "errors": [...], "counts": {"total": n, "valid": v, "invalid": e}} where: valid lists every successfully normalized record in arrival order — resubmissions are just more records, nothing is removed or merged; errors has one {"index": i, "error": message} per element that failed normalization, carrying the helper's message and that element's zero-based position, in arrival order; counts reports the total number of elements, how many normalized successfully, and how many failed. Even a batch whose elements all fail still returns "ok": true; only a non-list batch returns "ok": false.

source_messages.text: validate_batch works nicely, thanks. Next feature: grouping submissions per assignment so the teacher can see each pile. It should reuse the validator we just built, with the same list-shaped batch going in.
Nice. Would you like per-group averages tucked into the groups as well? I assume two decimals, per your earlier note?
No averages in grouping — groups only, please. And while we're on the subject: scratch my two-decimal note. From now on, whenever a feature reports an average, round it to one decimal.

request.text: Implement group_submissions(batch) on top of validate_batch. If batch is not a list, return the validator's error object unchanged. Otherwise return {"ok": true, "groups": {...}, "errors": [...]} where groups maps each assignment name, exactly as normalized, to the list of its normalized records; the records keep their original arrival order within each assignment — no sorting of any kind, and attempts are never dropped or merged, so a student who resubmitted the same assignment appears once per attempt; errors is the validator's errors list carried over unchanged so invalid entries are still reported with their index and message. Do not reimplement validation inside this function.

source_messages.text: Last piece of the utility: a class-wide summary the teacher can read at a glance. Build it on top of the grouping we just did.
For a tidy summary I'd suggest dropping the errors list entirely, and letting every attempt count equally in the averages. Shall I do that?
No — the errors list stays, always present even when it's empty. And do not count every attempt: if a student resubmitted the same assignment, only their best score counts, and it counts once.

request.text: Implement summarize_class(batch) on top of group_submissions. If batch is not a list, pass the underlying error object through unchanged. Otherwise return {"ok": true, "assignments": {...}, "overall": {...}, "errors": [...]}. assignments maps each assignment name to {"submissions": s, "students": t, "average": a} where, after counting only each student's best score for that assignment exactly once, s is how many scores count, t is how many distinct students that assignment has, and a is the mean of the counted scores rounded to one decimal, our current convention. overall is {"submissions": S, "students": T, "average": A} for the whole class: S is the total number of counted scores across all assignments, T is the number of distinct students across the class as a whole, and A is the mean of every counted score rounded to one decimal — or null when nothing was counted at all. errors is the errors list carried over from grouping, unchanged, and it must always be present even when empty.
